messages:
tomas: noticed a spike in streaming failures from hosted inference around 03:14 UTC. clients report stalled gRPC streams and 200→client timeouts. server logs show a bunch of RST_STREAMs.
karen: grafana alert fired: grpc_stream_error_rate up ~15% in last 10m. dashboard https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams
leo: looking at edge-proxy logs, seeing GOAWAY + RST_STREAM around the same time. a lot of short-lived connections followed by half-closed behavior.
infra-bot: deploy recorded: service/runtime promoted canary -> prod at 2026-03-18T03:10:12Z by ci-cd
tomas: this aligns w/ the gpu-scaleup event at 03:09 — nodes came up, traffic redistributed. possible NAT/ephemeral port churn? or LB mis-handling half-close.
karen: checking node metrics. SNAT ephemeral_port_used hit ~61k on a few egress NAT instances right at 03:11.
leo: also saw large initial response payloads from certain model variants after warmup, causing buffer bloat at the edge. could be WINDOW_UPDATE starvation when many streams open.
ryan: can someone paste a tcpdump snippet? curious whether we see FIN/ACK/GOAWAY patterns.
karen: here's a short snippet from the edge proxy host (sanitized):
```
20:14:33.123 IP 10.0.1.12.443 > 10.0.2.9.56789: Flags [P.], seq 1:345 ...
HTTP2 Frame: RST_STREAM (error code 2)
20:14:33.125 IP 10.0.1.12.443 > 10.0.2.9.56789: Flags [F.]
```
leo: that suggests the peer is explicitly resetting after partial frames. combined with high TIME_WAIT count we might be exhausting ephemeral ports and forcing connection churn.
tomas: can we get `ss -s` and `netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l` from the proxy? also what are ALB idle timeouts set to?
ryan: on one proxy host: TIME_WAIT = 56,200. ss shows many connections in CLOSE_WAIT and LAST_ACK.
karen: ALB idle timeout = 60s, envoy idle_timeout = 30s (we recently tightened envoy).
leo: envoy's aggressive idle timeout + ALB mismatch could cause half-close racing where client thinks stream persists but upstream closes socket — envoy then issues RST for active streams.
tomas: immediate mitigation: 1) rollback canary (we suspect runtime churn increases new connections), 2) relax envoy idle_timeout to match ALB, 3) expand NAT port range temporarily.
leo: opened PR to relax envoy timeout and add better connection reuse: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/402
infra-bot: rollback triggered for service/runtime: release-2026-03-18-0310 -> previous at 2026-03-18T03:25:09Z
karen: increased NAT ephemeral range on affected NATs and added short-term autoscale buffer. ephemeral_port_used back under 8k on measured instances.
ryan: after rollback + NAT tweak, grpc error rate recovered to baseline in ~6m. temporary fix seems effective.
tomas: leaving thread open for follow-up: add durable fixes — connection pooling in runtime, backpressure on large warmup payloads, harmonize idle timeouts, and a test for NAT port churn during scale events.
karen: filed follow-up ticket infra/EDGE-742 with checklist and owners.
leo: :thumbsup:
ryan: :eyes:
